title: Possessives 1: Mine and Yours (мой / твой)
description: Russian possessive pronouns agree with the noun they describe, just like adjectives. Today we drill the four forms of мой and твой across masculine, feminine, neuter, and plural.
descriptionRussian: Притяжательные местоимения согласуются с существительным, как прилагательные. Сегодня — четыре формы слов 'мой' и 'твой' в мужском, женском, среднем роде и во множественном числе.
intro: In English 'my' is one word that never moves. Russian makes it agree with whatever is being owned, so a single idea arrives in four shapes and you pick by looking at the noun rather than at yourself. That reversal is the whole difficulty, and it lasts about ten minutes. This book covers every word that behaves this way, starting with the two you will say most: the one for what is yours and the one for what belongs to a friend.
rules: The possessive pronoun мой ('my') has four forms agreeing with the noun: мой (m sg), моя (f sg), моё (n sg), мои (pl, any gender).
The possessive pronoun твой ('your', informal singular) has the parallel four forms: твой, твоя, твоё, твои. Same endings as мой.
One stem, four endings: мо- ('my') and тво- ('your') take -й (m sg), -я (f sg), -ё (n sg), -и (pl). The triggering question is always the same: which gender and number is the noun?
The plural ending is -и (мои, твои), one ending across all three genders. Russian collapses gender in the plural for possessives, just as it does for adjectives.
Use твой for one informal 'you' (a friend, family member, child). The polite or plural ваш is the topic of Lesson 2.
examples: Это мой брат. (This is my brother.) Брат is masculine singular, so the stem мо- takes -й: мой.
Это моя сестра. (This is my sister.) Сестра is feminine singular, so the stem мо- takes -я: моя.
Это моё письмо. (This is my letter.) Письмо is neuter singular, so the stem мо- takes -ё: моё.
Это мои родители. (These are my parents.) Родители is plural, so the stem мо- takes -и: мои.
Это твоя собака. (This is your dog.) Собака is feminine singular, so the stem тво- takes -я: твоя.
Это твои друзья. (These are your friends.) Друзья is plural, so the stem тво- takes -и: твои.

tables.title: Мой and Твой across the Four Forms

items.hint: Брат is one person. Which gender does it belong to?
items.explanation: Брат is masculine singular. The masculine form of the 'my' series is мой: the stem мо- plus the masculine ending -й.

items.hint: Сестра ends in -а. Which gender does that signal?
items.explanation: Сестра ends in -а, the standard feminine marker. The feminine form of the 'my' series is моя. The same моя attaches to any other feminine -а noun: моя книга, моя мама, моя комната.

items.hint: Письмо ends in -о. Which gender takes the -ё form (моё, твоё)?
items.explanation: Письмо ends in -о, the standard neuter marker. The neuter form of the 'my' series is моё. Same logic for моё окно, моё имя.

items.hint: Родители is plural. The plural form is the same across all genders.
items.explanation: Родители is plural (no Russian uses *родитель in everyday speech for both parents together). The plural form of the 'my' series is мои, and it works for any gender of plural noun: мои книги, мои дома, мои окна.

items.hint: Собака ends in -а: feminine singular. Match the ending you used on сестра earlier.
items.explanation: Собака is feminine singular. The feminine form of the 'your' series is твоя. The same pattern that produced моя сестра earlier produces твоя собака now.

items.hint: Друзья is plural. Pick the plural form of 'your'.
items.explanation: Друзья is the plural of друг. The plural form of the 'your' series is твои.

fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Книга is feminine singular. The feminine form of the 'my' series is моя.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: This is your phone - take it.
errorCorrection.explanation: Телефон is masculine (ends in a hard consonant), so the possessive takes the masculine form: твой. Твоя is the feminine form, so it cannot own телефон. The follow-up pronoun 'его' confirms the masculine gender.

errorCorrection.sentence: Это твой окно — не открывай его, на улице холодно.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: This is your window; don't open it, it's cold outside.
errorCorrection.explanation: Окно is neuter (-о ending), so 'your' takes the neuter form: твоё. The visual -о/-ё rhyme between the noun and the possessive is the cleanest cue Russian gives. Твой is the masculine form, so it does not match окно.

errorCorrection.sentence: У меня твой письмо, я случайно взяла его.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: I have your letter; I took it by accident.
errorCorrection.explanation: Письмо is neuter (ends in -о), so 'your' takes the neuter form: твоё письмо. Твой is the masculine form ('твой телефон'), so it does not match письмо. The neuter -ё on твоё mirrors the neuter -о on the noun.

minimalPairs.explanation: Дом is masculine singular, so the possessive takes the masculine -й form: мой. Моя would only fit a feminine noun like квартира.
Дети is plural. The plural form of the 'your' series is твои. The singular твой would only fit a single masculine noun like сын.

reviewVocab.definition: possessive pronoun (a word like мой, твой, наш, ваш that says who the noun belongs to)
reviewVocab.example: В выражении 'мой брат' слово 'мой' — притяжательное местоимение, указывающее на принадлежность.

reviewVocab.definition: agreement (the rule that the possessive takes endings matching the noun's gender and number)
reviewVocab.example: В словосочетании 'моя сестра' видно согласование: и существительное, и местоимение стоят в женском роде единственного числа.

reviewVocab.definition: number (singular or plural of the owned noun, which decides whether to use мой or мои)
reviewVocab.example: Слово 'родители' стоит во множественном числе, поэтому правильная форма местоимения — 'мои родители'.
